error_reason: The Planner agent repeatedly instructed the WebSurfer to open the same IMDb URL ('https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0106677/fullcredits/') without scrolling down or verifying if the character name was visible on the loaded page. The Planner failed to recognize that the task was effectively complete in Turn 7 (based on search results) or to instruct the WebSurfer to scroll to find the specific actor in the full credits list, resulting in the same page load action being performed six times (Turns 0, 4, 8, 10, 12, 14) with no extraction of the required data.

suggested_fix.fix_text: The Planner agent incorrectly inferred from Turn 13 that the specific role 'Benny O'Donnell' was found in prior web results, but the Turn 13 result was just a search query result that didn't show the specific actor role yet. The error stems from the Planner hallucinating confirmation instead of extracting the visible text from the previous turn (Turn 12) or the current load (Turns 8, 10, 14). The fix is to strictly instruct the agent to extract text from the currently visible viewport before concluding a fact, rather than assuming knowledge from a search snippet that may not be fully rendered or parsed.

probe_details.notes: The proposed error analysis claims the WebSurfer repeatedly opened the same URL (Turns 0, 4, 8, 10, 12, 14). However, examining the trace: Turn 0 searched 'Push Nevada creator', Turn 4 searched 'Ben Affleck Dazed and Confused role', Turn 8 opened the full credits URL, Turn 10 re-opened the full credits URL, Turn 12 searched again, and Turn 14 re-opened the full credits URL. While Turns 8, 10, and 14 did repeat the same action, Turn 0 and Turn 4 were different actions (searches). Furthermore, the analysis claims the Planner failed to recognize the task was complete in Turn 7, but Turn 7 explicitly stated the role had not been extracted yet. The actual failure mode is that the Planner hallucinated the discovery of 'Benny O'Donnell' in Turn 13 based on a search snippet without verifying it on the page, leading to unnecessary re-loading of the page in Turn 14. The proposed analysis misidentifies the specific nature of the repetition (citing Turn 0 as a repeat of the IMDb URL, which it wasn't) and slightly mischaracterizes the completeness check. The error type 'step_repetition' is partially applicable but the reasoning contains factual errors regarding the content of Turn 0 and Turn 4.
